decision_reason: A1 provides useful intensity, posture, impact and temporal contrasts, but exercising on a cross trainer differs from exercising on a stepper only in intensity. Adding upper-limb motion prominence offers a physically independent, potentially transferable distinction and helps describe rowing without inventing an unseen-specific attribute. Its predictability remains conditional on arm use. Other close pairs do not justify additional robust dimensions from the supplied semantics: standing and standing in an elevator still may be indistinguishable during constant-speed or stationary elevator intervals, and flat versus inclined treadmill walking does not warrant an assumed cadence or impact difference. A1 assignments are not validated measurements; in particular, lying orientation does not itself justify different smoothness.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: upper_limb_motion_prominence
attributes.definition: Degree of sustained upper-limb movement relative to the torso, excluding arm motion caused solely by whole-body transport.

levels.Low: Arms remain largely fixed relative to the torso, with little sustained upper-limb movement.
levels.Medium: Moderate sustained upper-limb movement relative to the torso.
levels.High: Pronounced sustained upper-limb movement relative to the torso.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotational energy across torso and limbs. It transfers from vigorous seen exercise to jumping and rowing, but speed, effort and technique can shift intensity; it should not alone separate cross trainer from stepper.
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in limb and torso motion, transferring from seen cyclic activities to unseen exercise. Harmonics, the choice of a full cycle versus an individual step, and self-selected exercise rate create ambiguity; absence of periodicity shares the Low state with slow repetition.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)
cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in acceleration, contrasting continuous exercise with repeated landing fluctuations. Descending stairs supplies a seen anchor for jumping. Speed and transmitted vibration can affect the evidence; static lying orientations do not intrinsically imply different smoothness.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief acceleration changes associated with foot contacts and landings, transferring from descending stairs and basketball to jumping. Landing technique and impact transmission introduce ambiguity. Elevator acceleration transitions may produce transients, but their occurrence within a window cannot be assumed.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative orientation across torso and limbs. Seen static postures and inclined treadmill walking anchor upright standing and flat walking. Dynamic acceleration, seated configurations and equipment-dependent lean complicate a global inclination estimate; lying on back and lying on right side need not differ on this scalar.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative torso and global body configuration. It supplies a useful distinction between rowing and relatively steady-posture cyclic exercise, with seen stairs and basketball providing examples of changing configurations. Rowing technique and window duration affect its degree; isolated limb cycling must not be mistaken for global postural change.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: rotational_motion: G2 supports sustained angular motion in the torso and limbs. Seen cycling and stepper exercise anchor substantial limb rotation in cross trainer exercise and rowing. Motion range and technique cause ambiguity, and aggregate rotation alone cannot identify which body region moves; the added upper-limb attribute addresses that limitation.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies, providing a broad distinction between locomotion and stationary exercise through seen walking and cycling. Predictability is limited: inertial signals do not establish constant velocity or absolute displacement, and treadmill limb travel differs from global progression. Elevator transport must not be treated as reliably observable during constant-speed intervals.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)
cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and consistency rather than repetition speed. Seen treadmill and stepper exercise anchor structured unseen exercise. Short windows and transitions can obscure regularity; steady stillness can also be highly predictable, so this attribute is not evidence of active repetition by itself.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: upper_limb_motion_prominence: G2, G3 and G14 support arm angular motion and multiaxial acceleration structure interpreted alongside torso motion. Pronounced arm excursions during rowing and moving-handle cross trainer use offer a contrast with predominantly lower-limb stepper and cycling exercise, independent of total intensity. Seen basketball and walking supply upper-limb motion anchors, while cycling supplies a relatively fixed-arm anchor. This is a coarse motion-amount distinction, not a fine-grained coordination claim. Fixed-handle cross trainer use, stepper arm use, restrained walking arm swing and torso-carried acceleration can weaken the contrast; no universal class separation is assumed.
contrast_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes describe motion amount, repetition rate, sustained fluctuations, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, global posture change, angular motion, translation, temporal predictability and upper-limb participation. Smoothness and impulsiveness distinguish sustained from brief rapid changes; cadence and regularity distinguish rate from consistency. Upper-limb motion prominence adds anatomical distribution rather than duplicating aggregate intensity or rotation, although these may covary. No extra elevator-specific attribute is introduced because passive constant-speed transport is not reliably identifiable with these IMUs. No new fine-grained phase, joint-angle or force attributes are justified by the supplied capability summary.
